title: Eleven People and a Bus Shelter
subtitle: 社区社会 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）
meta: 主题语境：社区社会（社会服务与人际沟通·社区与社会参与）　|　核心词汇：interest　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 interest 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Our village has eleven people on the council and two hundred and forty residents, and the gap between those numbers is the whole of local politics. Interest, my mother said, is the cheapest thing a young person can offer. I joined at nineteen because an ① interest in the bus shelter seemed harmless, and because a man on the ② interest of the parish had told my mother it would look well on a form. He was right, and I am not proud of it.

The shelter had been condemned in 2009 and demolished in 2011 and not replaced, which meant that eleven pensioners waited for the ③ interest of nobody in particular at a gate on the main road. What the council called the public ④ interest was, in practice, a question about insurance. What the pensioners called it was cold.

I learned the vocabulary quickly. A declared ⑤ interest is a thing you own, or a relative who does, and must say so before speaking; an undeclared one is the same thing said afterwards, by somebody else. There were also ⑥ interests on the loan the council had taken out for a footpath nobody used, and they were larger than the footpath.

The shelter was finally built in 2014, eleven feet long, paid for by a grant and by a man who had ⑦ interested himself in the matter for three years and had never once come to a meeting. He simply wrote cheques and asked for nothing. The council, which had spent those three years ⑧ interesting itself in procedure, was mildly offended by him, and I have thought about that ever since.

I resigned in 2016. What I had lost, slowly and completely, was not ⑨ interest in the village but interest in the meetings, and those are different things. The shelter is still there, and in the ⑩ interest of full disclosure I should say that I have never once waited in it: I was nineteen, I had a car, and I did not need it. That, I now think, is exactly the problem.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 兴趣；关注（interest in）
B. n. 利益；利害关系（a declared interest）
C. n. 利息（on a loan）
D. n. 好处；益处；福利（the interest of）
E. 固定搭配：the public interest 公共利益
F. 固定搭配：in the interest of 为了；出于……的考虑
G. v. 使……关注；使介入（interest oneself in）
H. 固定搭配：take/have an interest in 对……感兴趣；关心

items.q: an interest in the bus shelter seemed harmless
on the interest of the parish
waited for the interest of nobody in particular
What the council called the public interest
A declared interest is a thing you own
There were also interests on the loan
had interested himself in the matter
spent those three years interesting itself in procedure
not interest in the village but interest in the meetings
in the interest of full disclosure

answers.why: an interest in 是固定搭配，意为“对……感兴趣、关心”，说这份关心看起来无害。
in the interest of 结构中的 interest 指“利益、好处”，此处说“代表教区的利益”。
同样指“利益、关照”，说十一位老人为了无人特别关照的事在大路口等车。
the public interest 是固定搭配，意为“公共利益”。
a declared interest 意为“已申报的利害关系”，即你或亲属拥有的东西。
interest 指贷款的“利息”，说那条没人走的小路的贷款利息比路本身还高。
interest oneself in 是动词用法，意为“使自己关注、介入”，说那人关注此事三年。
同样作动词，说议会那三年只关心程序问题。
interest in 意为“对……的兴趣”，说失去的不是对村子的兴趣而是对开会的兴趣。
in the interest of 意为“为了、出于……的考虑”，此处用于坦白说明。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 我十九岁加入议会，因为对候车亭的关心看似无害。（interest in）
议会所说的公共利益，实际上是个保险问题。（the public interest）
所谓已申报的利害关系，就是你或亲属拥有的东西。（a declared interest）
那笔贷款的利息比那条小路本身还贵。（interest）
有个人关注了这件事三年，却从未出席过一次会议。（interest oneself in）
为了充分披露，我该说：我从未在亭子里等过车。（in the interest of）
answers: Interest, my mother said, is the cheapest thing a young person can offer. I joined at nineteen because an interest in the bus shelter seemed harmless.
What the council called the public interest was, in practice, a question about insurance.
A declared interest is a thing you own, or a relative who does.
The interest on that loan was larger than the footpath itself.
One man interested himself in the matter for three years and never came to a meeting.
In the interest of full disclosure, I have never once waited in the shelter.
